silhouette.reason: Heavy jaw, brow shelf, thick neck, crest and tusks read as an orc from the front and 3/4; from behind it is a bald green human with a crest.
fixes: push the trapezius higher and the head forward (hunched stance); bigger, wider-set tusks

proportions.reason: Declared ratios hold (jaw, eye spacing); the mid-face still reads too human between the cheekbones.
fixes: flatten the nose bridge further and widen the nostril flare; lower the eyes under the brow shelf

materials.reason: Vertex colour on the plain strip: green skin zones separate by hue but not by roughness or subsurface; the crest is the same material as the skin, so it reads as sculpted clay; tusks separate by hue only.
fixes: a skin strip with subsurface-like roughness/sheen and a hair strip with anisotropic sheen for the crest
glossier, slightly yellowed ivory on the tusks with a darker root

detail.reason: Primary and secondary forms come from a real anatomical base (lids, nasolabial area, lips, ear helix, clavicles, sternocleidomastoid), but there is no tertiary layer (pores, wrinkles) and the hair is evenly spaced grooves.
fixes: LOD0 wrinkle/pore displacement on the subdivided base driven by age
varied lock widths and a parting instead of evenly spaced grooves

wear.reason: Pristine: seeded asymmetry and age/weight knobs are the only story; no scars, stubble, blemishes, sun-darkened skin or dirt.
fixes: seeded scar/blemish marks in vertex colour
stubble shadow on the jaw and age-driven darkening under the eyes

lod.reason: LOD2 keeps the crest, jaw and outline, but the face in sheet.png breaks into dark blotches around the eyes and mouth and the tusks fragment.
fixes: authored low-poly topology for LOD2; keep the tusks as separate cones at LOD2

technical.reason: QA PASS at every LOD; 83.6k / 29.5k / 8.1k tris; teeth declared rest (no gums), tusks rooted in the jaw.
fixes: model a gum strip so the teeth can be grown instead of rest
